extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: FLORES-101 is a multilingual machine translation evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia (WikiNews, WikiJunior, WikiVoyage) and professionally translated into 101 languages. It supports many-to-many multilingual evaluation across 10,100 language pairs, with multilingually aligned translations and rich metadata for document-level and multimodal translation tasks.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.inLanguage: af, am, ar, hy, as, ast, az, be, bn, bs, bg, my, ca, ceb, zh, hr, cs, da, nl, et, tl, fi, fr, ff, gl, lg, ka, de, el, gu, ha, he, hi, hu, is, ig, id, ga, it
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources (Wikinews, Wikijunior, WikiVoyage) in English, then professionally translated into 101 languages through a multi-round translation workflow involving Language Service Providers (LSPs) with automatic and human quality checks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English sentences extracted from Wikimedia sources: Wikinews (international news articles), Wikijunior (nonfiction books for children), and WikiVoyage (travel guide articles). Total of 3001 sentences from 842 articles.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were translated by professional Language Service Providers (LSPs). Translations underwent automatic checks; failures were sent back for re-translation. Passing translations were sent to a second LSP for human evaluation. If quality was insufficient (threshold: 90% based on human evaluation), translations were returned for re-translation, with multiple rounds possible. Sentence selection was performed manually by 10 annotators who selected contiguous sentences from articles and labeled them by sub-topic.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Language Service Providers (LSPs) — two different LSPs used per language (one for translation, one for human evaluation)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation scores were used as quality thresholds; all 101 languages met an initial threshold of 90% quality based on human evaluation. About 50% of languages scored above 95%. Error categories were analyzed: mistranslation was the largest error category; other categories included register, grammar, and punctuation. Domain-level variation in errors was also examined.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 10 annotators (for sentence selection): 6 male and 4 female; roles included researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; from regions including East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic checks were applied to translations before human evaluation, though specific tools are not named.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Sentences are sourced from English Wikipedia, which may introduce translationese effects. The sentence selection was performed by 10 annotators with specific demographic characteristics (6 male, 4 female, from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America), which may introduce selection bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: All source sentences are from English Wikipedia, meaning non-English source sentences are produced by human translators (translationese). The benchmark is limited to 101 languages, and low-resource languages may have limited qualified professional translators, affecting translation quality consistency.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to benefit the majority of the world's population who speak low-resource languages by enabling better evaluation and improvement of machine translation systems for those languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use case is evaluation of machine translation systems, including many-to-many multilingual translation across 10,100 language pairs. Additional use cases include document-level translation, multimodal translation via images, sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand the number of languages covered in FLORES-101 and make the test set available to community efforts and shared tasks such as those from the Workshop on Machine Translation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Paragraph location selection was balanced equally across the corpus (beginning, middle, end of articles), with roughly one third of paragraphs sampled from each location. Sentences were sourced equally from three domains: Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage (one third each).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia sources (Wikinews, Wikijunior, WikiVoyage). Selection involved manually choosing 3-5 contiguous sentences per article, avoiding very short or malformed sentences, selecting one paragraph per document. Metadata including Wikipedia URL, topic, boolean flags for linked entities and images were extracted. Sentences were manually labeled by sub-topic. Translations underwent automatic quality checks (spBLEU-based comparison against commercial engines) and human quality evaluation with a translation quality score threshold of 90%. Translations failing checks were sent back for re-translation.

If these checks fail, translations are sent back for re-translation. If the automatic checks pass, translations are sent to another LSP for human evaluation. If the quality is not sufficient, translations are sent back to the original translation LSP for re-translation.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: By translating the same set of English sentences in more than hundred languages, we enable evaluation of multilingual MT with the only caveat that source sentences not in English are produced by human translators. While translationese (or overly literal or awkward translations) has known idiosyncrasies... Obtaining high translation quality in low-resource languages is difﬁcult because the translation job relies on the skill of a small set of translators.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: the majority of the world's population speak low-resource languages and would beneﬁt from improvements in translation quality on their native languages... FLORES-101 supports many-to-many evaluation, meaning any of 10,100 language directions can be evaluated... supports the measurement of traditionally neglected regionally-relevant pairs such as Xhosa-Zulu, Vietnamese-Thai, and Spanish-Aymara

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Beyond translation, FLORES-101 can be used to evaluate tasks such as sentence and document classiﬁcation, language identiﬁcation, and multilingual domain adaptation... we also support evaluation of machine translation at the document level. With the additional meta-data, we also enable evaluation of multimodal machine translation.
